prompt: What does a rule like *Do not use the category other unless you have to* leave unsaid?
hint: A prohibition marks one wrong thing.

choices.text: That the model is allowed to use the category other in the first place, which the label list says already
choices.why: That much is said; what is missing is when and what instead.

choices.text: When you have to, and which category to use instead
choices.why: Right: it marks what to avoid and leaves the target unstated.

choices.text: How long the summary is
choices.why: Other rules deal with that.

choices.text: The JSON format
choices.why: The format is stated above the rules.

prompt: According to `pl lint`, how many of the thirteen rules in `v8-rules.txt` say only what not to do?
hint: `rules say only what not to do`.

prompt: Why did `pl lint` not report lines 12 and 13 as a contradiction?

choices.text: It matches words, and *never* and *always* are not on its list of opposite instructions
choices.why: Right: it reported them only as shouting.

choices.text: The two lines are not next to each other
choices.why: They are adjacent, and adjacency is not what it checks.

choices.text: It reads the first ten lines
choices.why: It reported line 20.

choices.text: They do not conflict
choices.why: They do, on a question about money.

prompt: `t22` asks whether a gift card and a credit card can be used on one order. What urgency does the rule list give it?
hint: It is a question, and it is about money.

choices.text: Low, because line 12 comes first and the earlier rule wins
choices.why: The prompt says nothing about which rule wins.

choices.text: High, because capital letters outrank everything else in a prompt
choices.why: Both rules are in capitals.

choices.text: Both high and never high
choices.why: Right: two absolutes that cannot both hold.

choices.text: Normal
choices.why: Neither rule mentions normal.

choices.text: By a list of keywords that have to appear in the message
choices.why: It names no keywords.

choices.text: By an example message and its full JSON answer
choices.why: It has no examples.

choices.text: By the urgency it usually has
choices.why: Urgency is described separately.

choices.text: By who answers it
choices.why: Right: the accounts desk, the warehouse, whoever runs the website.

prompt: How does the guide settle the urgency of `t22`, where the rule list contradicts itself?

choices.text: Nobody is out of pocket and the question will keep for a day, so it is low, as the labeller said
choices.why: Right: one principle covers both rules and their collision.

choices.text: It adds a rule about questions
choices.why: It has no rule about questions.

choices.text: It marks it high
choices.why: Nobody has lost anything yet.

choices.text: It leaves it to the model
choices.why: It gives the model a principle to apply.

prompt: `pl tokens` counts `v8-rules.txt` at 199 tokens and `v8-guide.txt` at 246. How many tokens longer is the guide?
Lesson 2 cut 98 tokens from a prompt and lost nothing; the guide is 47 tokens longer than the rules. Why is that consistent?

choices.text: Because token counts in this lab are approximate, so forty-seven extra tokens sit inside the counter's margin of error
choices.why: The counts are exact for the lab's tokenizer.

choices.text: The lines cut there decided no answer; each line of the guide carries a reason
choices.why: Right: the test of a line is whether it changes an answer.

choices.text: Short prompts are better
choices.why: Length is not the test.

choices.text: It is not; cut the guide
choices.why: The guide's lines are not the kind lesson 2 cut.

prompt: Over seventy cases the rules passed 45 and the guide 43, with `p = 0.727`. What is the right report?
hint: A difference that chance produces three times in four.

choices.text: The rule list is better by two messages and should be kept
choices.why: Two messages, at p = 0.727, are noise.

choices.text: Explanations do not work on language models of any kind
choices.why: The stand-in is not a language model, and one run proves no such thing.

choices.text: No difference detected on seventy cases
choices.why: Right: neither better nor worse, as far as this run can tell.

choices.text: The guide is worse
choices.why: Not by any test that separates it from chance.

prompt: Why could the stand-in not reward the guide's explanations?
hint: What does it take from a prompt?

choices.text: It does not read meaning: it sorts by keywords and judges urgency from a short list of phrases
choices.why: Right: a reason is not among the words it scans for.

choices.text: The guide is too long for it
choices.why: Length does not stop it reading.

choices.text: It was not running
choices.why: It answered all 140 calls.

choices.text: Seventy is too few
choices.why: With identical categories, no number of cases would show a difference.

prompt: What does the lesson say about how this comparison comes out on a real model?

choices.text: That explanations win by around ten points, as the vendors report
choices.why: The lesson quotes no such figure, and the vendors' guidance is not a measurement.

choices.text: That real models ignore explanations just as the stand-in does
choices.why: The stand-in's limit is the stand-in's.

choices.text: That rules win on short messages and reasons on long ones
choices.why: Nothing in the lesson says so.

choices.text: No number until you run it
choices.why: Right: the comparison is the experiment.

prompt: Of the 70 messages, only the ___ that changed between the two runs carry evidence about which prompt is better.
hint: Three one way, five the other.

prompt: Read as written, which category does the rule list give `h01`, a refund paid to the wrong card after a return?

choices.text: billing, by line 17, which is also what the labeller decided for this message
choices.why: Line 18 is the more specific rule, and it says returns.

choices.text: returns, by line 18, while the person who labelled it said billing
choices.why: Right: a confident wrong answer for a case nobody listed.

choices.text: account
choices.why: No rule points there.

choices.text: other
choices.why: Line 10 discourages it, and no rule points there.

prompt: What does a reason written beside a rule give the person who maintains the prompt?
hint: Think of line 19 of the rules.

choices.text: A guarantee that the model follows the rule on each message from now on
choices.why: A reason guarantees nothing about the model.

choices.text: Permission to delete the other rules without testing them first
choices.why: Deleting still needs a test.

choices.text: A way to tell when it no longer applies
choices.why: Right, and then to delete it with a test instead of a guess.

choices.text: Fewer tokens
choices.why: A reason adds tokens.

prompt: Where does the lesson say reasons belong in a prompt?

choices.text: On every line, including the label lists and the JSON shape
choices.why: Contracts are stated, not argued.

choices.text: In a separate document that the model is never shown
choices.why: The model is one of the two readers.

choices.text: In the test set beside the expected answers
choices.why: They belong in the prompt, where both readers meet them.

choices.text: Where judgement is needed
choices.why: Right: which desk, how urgent, what the summary is for.

prompt: Which of these does the lesson cite from Anthropic's prompt engineering documentation? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: Give the context and the motivation behind an instruction
choices.why: Yes.

choices.text: Say what to do, not only what not to do
choices.why: Yes.

choices.text: Write the most important rules in capitals
choices.why: The lesson cites nothing of the kind.

choices.text: A measured gain of a stated size
choices.why: The lesson says it is guidance, not a measurement.

prompt: After `h01` fails, a colleague adds a fourteenth rule: *A refund to the wrong card is billing.* What does the lesson suggest instead?
hint: The next unlisted case is coming.

choices.text: Explain what billing is for, the desk that puts money back on cards, so the next unlisted case is covered too
choices.why: Right: a reason reaches cases a rule does not name.

choices.text: Keep it; fourteen rules are fine
choices.why: Each new rule moves the edge to the next case.

choices.text: Put the new rule in capitals
choices.why: Shouting ranks rules; it explains nothing.

choices.text: Delete line 18
choices.why: Line 18 is right for most returned books; what is missing is the reason.
